question: Explain the circumstances in which an auditor issues a qualified opinion, an adverse opinion and a disclaimer of opinion under SA 705.
sources: SA 705 Modifications to the Opinion in the Independent Auditor's Report

points.label: When the opinion is modified
points.description: The auditor modifies the opinion when the financial statements as a whole are materially misstated, or when sufficient appropriate evidence cannot be obtained to conclude that they are free of material misstatement.
points.basis: SA 705, circumstances when a modification is required

points.label: Meaning of pervasive
points.description: Effects are pervasive when they are not confined to specific items, or form a substantial part of the financial statements, or are basic to users' understanding of them.

points.label: Qualified opinion
points.description: Given when misstatements are material but not pervasive, or when evidence cannot be obtained and the possible effects are material but not pervasive.

points.label: Adverse opinion
points.description: Given when, after obtaining sufficient appropriate evidence, misstatements are both material and pervasive.

points.label: Disclaimer of opinion
points.description: Given when the auditor cannot obtain sufficient appropriate evidence and the possible effects of undetected misstatements could be both material and pervasive.
